title: Brush teeth, read, then go to bed
subtitle: Repeat a familiar bedtime routine
description: Help your child brush their teeth, read together, and go to bed at a regular time.

title: Dim the bedroom lights before bed
subtitle: Use a dim night-light if needed
description: For ages 3–18, reduce bedroom light at bedtime; use a dim, warm-coloured night-light if needed.

ageVersions.title: Help your child set up dim lighting for bedtime
ageVersions.subtitle: Practise together; let your child take the next step
ageVersions.description: Let them help choose a dim, warm night-light if needed.

ageVersions.title: Have your teen prepare a dim, quiet bedroom before sleep
ageVersions.subtitle: Plan together and let your teen take more responsibility
ageVersions.description: Discuss light, noise and devices that make settling harder.

ageVersions.title: Let your teen identify and reduce bedroom distractions that disturb sleep
ageVersions.subtitle: Support self-management and remain available to help
ageVersions.description: Review practical changes together, such as light, noise and device placement.

title: Put screens away an hour before your child’s bedtime
subtitle: Charge devices outside the bedroom
description: For ages 3–18, stop screens at least an hour before bed and keep devices outside the bedroom overnight.

ageVersions.title: Agree where your child will put devices an hour before bed
ageVersions.subtitle: Practise together; let your child take the next step
ageVersions.description: Choose an overnight charging place outside the bedroom together.

ageVersions.title: Ask your teen to set a reminder for their screen-free wind-down
ageVersions.subtitle: Plan together and let your teen take more responsibility
ageVersions.description: Agree an hour without screens before bed and charge devices outside the bedroom.

ageVersions.title: Have your teen plan when to finish online activities before bedtime
ageVersions.subtitle: Support self-management and remain available to help
ageVersions.description: Review whether their plan protects the screen-free hour and keeps devices out overnight.

title: Take your child outside in the morning daylight
subtitle: Include daylight in the morning routine
description: Encourage time outdoors in natural light, especially in the morning. Choose a safe activity that suits your child.

title: Keep bedtime and waking times regular
subtitle: Follow a similar schedule on weekends
description: For ages 3–18, keep bedtimes and wake-up times within 1–2 hours across the week.

ageVersions.title: Choose regular bedtime and wake-up times with your child
ageVersions.subtitle: Practise together; let your child take the next step
ageVersions.description: Help them follow a similar schedule on school days and weekends.

ageVersions.title: Plan a sleep schedule with your teen around their school start time
ageVersions.subtitle: Plan together and let your teen take more responsibility
ageVersions.description: Discuss enough sleep and let them choose a wind-down habit to try.

ageVersions.title: Ask your teen to review whether their sleep schedule leaves them rested
ageVersions.subtitle: Support self-management and remain available to help
ageVersions.description: Support them in adjusting bedtime and wake time around their commitments.

title: Remind your child to use the toilet before bed if they wet the bed
subtitle: Keep the toilet easy to reach at night
description: Encourage a toilet visit before bed and make the toilet easy to reach at night. This is situation-specific guidance, not a requirement for every child.

title: Listen to your teen’s worries before settling for sleep
subtitle: Make time earlier in the day for longer conversations
description: Acknowledge worries that come up at bedtime. If they need a longer discussion, arrange time during the day to talk them through.

title: Include fruit, vegetables and whole grains in family meals
subtitle: Offer variety across the week
description: Offer fruit, vegetables and whole-grain foods across meals, rather than repeatedly relying on the same foods.

ageVersions.title: Let your child help choose fruit and vegetables for family meals
ageVersions.subtitle: Practise together; let your child take the next step
ageVersions.description: Choose a variety together while you provide balanced options.

ageVersions.title: Ask your teen to include fruit, vegetables and whole grains in meal planning
ageVersions.subtitle: Plan together and let your teen take more responsibility
ageVersions.description: Let them help choose what the family shops for.

ageVersions.title: Support your teen in choosing varied meals when eating away from home
ageVersions.subtitle: Support self-management and remain available to help
ageVersions.description: Discuss choices they enjoy and how to include different food groups.

title: Let your child stop eating when full
subtitle: Offer food without pressure to finish
description: Provide meals and snacks at predictable times, and let your child decide whether they are hungry and when they have eaten enough.

title: Share a relaxed family meal
subtitle: Make room for friendly conversation
description: Eat together when possible and keep mealtime conversation pleasant, without arguments or lectures.

title: Vary the protein foods you serve your child
subtitle: Include options such as beans, eggs, fish or lean meat
description: Include protein foods such as beans, eggs, fish or lean meat as part of varied meals.

title: Offer water instead of sugary drinks
subtitle: Make water an everyday option
description: Offer water in place of soda and other sugary drinks.

title: Avoid comparing your teen’s body with anyone else’s
subtitle: Model respect for different body shapes
description: Avoid comparisons about your child’s body or your own. Talk about caring for the body without ranking people by their size or appearance.

title: Offer new foods alongside familiar ones
subtitle: For toddlers learning to enjoy different foods
description: Serve a small amount of a new food with familiar foods. Offer it again on another occasion without bargaining over bites.

title: Walk or cycle together on short trips
subtitle: Build movement into family travel
description: When practical, walk or cycle together for short journeys instead of taking the car.

title: Make time for your preschooler to run, dance and play throughout the day
subtitle: Spread movement across the day
description: For ages 2–4, offer varied movement totalling at least 3 hours across the day. At ages 3–4, include at least an hour of more energetic play. Adapt activities to ability and any individual healthcare advice.

title: Plan time for your child to play sports, cycle or dance
subtitle: Choose activities they enjoy and can manage
description: For ages 5–18, build varied activity into the week. General guidance is an average of at least 60 minutes of moderate or vigorous activity daily; adapt the plan for disability or health needs using individual advice.

ageVersions.title: Help your child choose active games and sports across the week
ageVersions.subtitle: Practise together; let your child take the next step
ageVersions.description: Offer varied, enjoyable movement suited to their abilities.

ageVersions.title: Plan a varied activity week with your teen around their interests
ageVersions.subtitle: Plan together and let your teen take more responsibility
ageVersions.description: Include enjoyable activity that develops fitness, movement skills, muscles and bones.

ageVersions.title: Support your teen in managing their own weekly activity plan
ageVersions.subtitle: Support self-management and remain available to help
ageVersions.description: Help them balance enjoyable activity with commitments and adapt for health or disability needs.

title: Practise throwing and catching through play
subtitle: For young children developing movement skills
description: Play throwing-and-catching games suited to your child’s age and ability.

title: Let your child choose their own outdoor game
subtitle: Supervise without directing every part of play
description: Offer a safe outdoor space and let your child decide how to play. Stay available and supervise as their age and the setting require.

title: Encourage your child to move after sitting for a long time
subtitle: Break up long seated activities
description: During long periods of sitting, encourage a movement break such as walking or dancing, adapted to your child’s abilities.

title: Help your child brush their teeth morning and night
subtitle: Use fluoride toothpaste and help while they learn
description: Brush twice daily for two minutes with fluoride toothpaste. Use a rice-grain amount under age 3 and a pea-sized amount at ages 3–6. Help young children brush and supervise until they can brush thoroughly.

title: Wash hands before eating and after the toilet
subtitle: Use soap, scrub, rinse and dry
description: Help your child wash with soap and water before eating and after using the toilet, scrubbing for at least 20 seconds.

title: Apply sunscreen to your child’s exposed skin before going outdoors
subtitle: Use shade and protective clothing too
description: Use broad-spectrum sunscreen, SPF 15 or higher, on exposed skin 15–30 minutes before going outside. Reapply every two hours and after swimming, sweating or towel drying. Use shade, a hat and protective clothing too.

title: Pack water in your child’s school bag
subtitle: Make drinking water available at school
description: Fill a reusable bottle with water and put it with your child’s school things.

title: Help your teen change out of sweaty sports clothes
subtitle: Put used clothes with the laundry
description: After exercise, encourage your teen to change into clean clothes and put sweaty clothing aside for washing.

title: Help your teen make time to wash their body each day
subtitle: Discuss body odour kindly and privately
description: Help your teen establish a daily shower or bath routine, including washing underarms and feet. Discuss deodorant privately if needed.

title: Practise slow breathing with your child while they are calm
subtitle: Breathe in gently and let the breath out slowly
description: In a quiet moment, practise breathing slowly in through the nose and out through the mouth. Start with one breath for younger children.

title: Help your child spot tense muscles or clenched fists when anger starts
subtitle: Recognise their own early warning signs
description: Help your child recognise their own warning signs, such as tense muscles, clenched fists or a faster heartbeat.

title: Help your child put their feelings into words when they are upset
subtitle: Connect the emotion to what happened
description: Listen to what happened and help your young child find words for the emotion they are experiencing.

title: Help your child choose what to do when they start feeling angry
subtitle: Practise a response while they are calm
description: Together choose a response, such as walking away to a safe place or talking to a trusted adult. Practise before anger builds.

ageVersions.title: Choose an anger-coping strategy with your child and practise it calmly
ageVersions.subtitle: Practise together; let your child take the next step
ageVersions.description: Try stepping away safely or talking to a trusted adult.

ageVersions.title: Help your teen match an anger warning sign to a coping response
ageVersions.subtitle: Plan together and let your teen take more responsibility
ageVersions.description: Let them choose a response they can use before anger escalates.

ageVersions.title: Ask your teen to review which anger-coping responses help them
ageVersions.subtitle: Support self-management and remain available to help
ageVersions.description: Support adjustments to their plan and seeking help when anger remains difficult.

title: After your child calms down, practise asking for a toy instead of hitting
subtitle: Teach an alternative after the upset has passed
description: When everyone is calm, explain that anger is allowed but hitting hurts. Help your child practise words for asking or taking turns.

title: Stay calmly nearby while your upset child settles
subtitle: Check safety and wait before discussing behaviour
description: Stay close enough to keep your child safe while the strong feeling passes. Offer calm support; discuss what happened after they can listen.

title: Put your phone away and spend time playing or talking with your child
subtitle: Give them your undivided attention
description: Set aside one-to-one time with distractions switched off. Join your child in play or conversation about something they enjoy.

ageVersions.title: Let your child choose an activity for uninterrupted time together
ageVersions.subtitle: Practise together; let your child take the next step
ageVersions.description: Join their interest and put distracting devices away.

ageVersions.title: Ask your teen how they would like to spend one-to-one time with you
ageVersions.subtitle: Plan together and let your teen take more responsibility
ageVersions.description: Make space for their interests without turning the time into questioning.

ageVersions.title: Agree with your teen on time together that fits both your schedules
ageVersions.subtitle: Support self-management and remain available to help
ageVersions.description: Let them suggest the activity and protect that time from distractions.

title: Let your child finish speaking, then repeat back what you understood
subtitle: Give them a chance to correct you
description: Listen without interrupting. Paraphrase what your child said and let them explain if you misunderstood.

title: Ask your teen whether they want listening or help solving a problem
subtitle: Let them say what support would help
description: Listen first, then ask whether your child wants you to listen or help them work through a solution.

title: Ask your child what they enjoyed or found difficult at school
subtitle: Listen to their experiences with friends and learning
description: Ask about friends, enjoyable experiences and difficulties, then listen to how your child feels about them.

title: Tell your toddler one specific thing to do at a time
subtitle: Get their attention and use a calm voice
description: Give a short direction naming the action, such as putting a toy in its box. Wait for your child to respond before adding another instruction.

title: Warn your child five minutes before playtime ends
subtitle: Explain which activity comes next
description: Before ending play, give a five-minute warning and explain what will happen next.

title: Compare possible solutions with your teen before making a difficult decision
subtitle: Talk through options and their likely outcomes
description: Name the problem together, list possible solutions and discuss the advantages and disadvantages. Agree on a workable choice and check later how it went.

ageVersions.title: List possible solutions to an everyday problem with your child
ageVersions.subtitle: Practise together; let your child take the next step
ageVersions.description: Compare options together and agree one to try.

ageVersions.title: Ask your teen to suggest solutions before you offer yours
ageVersions.subtitle: Plan together and let your teen take more responsibility
ageVersions.description: Discuss consequences and agree how to try their chosen option.

ageVersions.title: Let your teen lead a decision and review how their choice worked
ageVersions.subtitle: Support self-management and remain available to help
ageVersions.description: Be a sounding board while they compare options, act and reflect.

title: Teach your child to help set the table before meals
subtitle: Start with items they can carry safely
description: Show your child where table items go, then let them help. Choose items and support to suit their abilities.

title: Describe what your toddler is doing as they play
subtitle: Put their actions into simple words
description: While watching your child play, describe their actions, shapes or colours without turning it into a quiz. Follow what interests them.

title: Help your child practise putting on their own clothes
subtitle: Break dressing into manageable steps
description: Offer easy-to-manage clothes and help with the steps your child cannot yet do. Let them practise at their own pace.

title: Help your child wipe up a small spill they made
subtitle: Show them how to use a cloth
description: For a small, safe spill, show your child how to wipe it up and help as needed. An adult handles hot liquids, broken glass and other hazards.

title: Practise a greeting with your child before they meet new children
subtitle: Rehearse a greeting together at home
description: If meeting children feels daunting, role-play saying hello and asking about a game before the visit.

title: Teach your child to put dirty clothes in the laundry basket
subtitle: Show them where used clothes belong
description: Put a laundry basket within reach and show your child where to put clothes that need washing. Help younger children.

title: Put toys away together
subtitle: Start with a manageable chore for young children
description: Help your young child put toys away, giving them support as they learn the task.

title: Let your child help measure ingredients while you cook
subtitle: Help them fill measuring cups and compare amounts.
description: During a suitable cooking activity, help your child fill and level measuring cups and compare quantities.

ageVersions.title: Let your child follow a simple recipe with your supervision
ageVersions.subtitle: Practise together; let your child take the next step
ageVersions.description: Help them measure, read the steps and practise safe preparation.

ageVersions.title: Help your teen prepare a simple family meal from a recipe
ageVersions.subtitle: Plan together and let your teen take more responsibility
ageVersions.description: Agree what they can handle safely and stay available for unfamiliar steps.

ageVersions.title: Let your teen plan, shop for and cook a simple family meal
ageVersions.subtitle: Support self-management and remain available to help
ageVersions.description: Agree the budget and provide support for equipment or techniques they have not learned.

title: Agree who does each household job
subtitle: Make responsibilities clear
description: Discuss suitable chores together and use a list or chart to show who is responsible and when each job needs doing.

ageVersions.title: Let your child choose a household job and agree when it gets done
ageVersions.subtitle: Practise together; let your child take the next step
ageVersions.description: Write down the responsibility and practise the job together.

ageVersions.title: Agree which household jobs your teen will manage independently
ageVersions.subtitle: Plan together and let your teen take more responsibility
ageVersions.description: Clarify the result and timing, and teach unfamiliar steps.

ageVersions.title: Review your teen’s household responsibilities around school and work commitments
ageVersions.subtitle: Support self-management and remain available to help
ageVersions.description: Let them plan when to complete agreed jobs and raise scheduling conflicts.

title: Let your child help clear their plate after a meal
subtitle: Use dishes they can carry safely
description: Show your child where used dishes go and help them carry suitable items after eating.

title: Let your child hear you thank someone for helping
subtitle: Name what you appreciated
description: Model gratitude by thanking someone for a specific helpful action while your child is present.

title: Compare prices and features with your teen before choosing a phone plan
subtitle: Discuss which option fits the family’s needs and budget.
description: When choosing a phone plan with your teen, compare features and costs together against the family’s needs and budget.

title: Invite your child to describe the pictures while you read together
subtitle: Build on their comments without turning reading into a quiz.
description: With a preschooler, invite comments about the pictures, build on their answers and follow their interest. Keep it enjoyable rather than questioning them on every page.

title: Explore the answer together when your child asks how something works
subtitle: Observe, look it up or try a simple experiment.
description: When your child wonders about something, explore the answer together through observation or a simple experiment. You do not need to know the answer beforehand.

title: Let your child draw or paint without copying a sample
subtitle: Provide materials and let them choose what to make.
description: For young children, provide blank paper and suitable drawing or craft materials. Let them explore without copying a model or having their work corrected.

title: Create a list together of things your child can do when bored
subtitle: Choose activities they enjoy; use pictures for younger children.
description: Create a list together based on your child’s interests. Use pictures for younger children, and let them refer to it during free time.

title: Meet as a family each week to discuss plans and concerns
subtitle: Give everyone a turn to speak and write down agreements.
description: For families with school-age children, meet at a regular weekly time, let everyone speak without interruption, and record agreements. Keep reprimands out of the meeting.

title: Help your child draw or photograph something they noticed in nature
subtitle: Record what interested them so you can revisit it together.
description: When something interests your child—a plant, the moon or changing leaves—help them record their observations so they can revisit them.

title: Check your child’s homework deadlines together
subtitle: Put assignments and due dates in a planner
description: Review upcoming assignments with your child and record due dates. Help them decide when to work on each task.

ageVersions.title: Help your child enter homework deadlines in their own planner
ageVersions.subtitle: Practise together; let your child take the next step
ageVersions.description: Let them record assignments while you check the entries together.

ageVersions.title: Have your teen plan the week’s assignments around other commitments
ageVersions.subtitle: Plan together and let your teen take more responsibility
ageVersions.description: Review their calendar together and help spot clashes.

ageVersions.title: Let your teen manage assignment deadlines and flag overload early
ageVersions.subtitle: Support self-management and remain available to help
ageVersions.description: Ask them to identify competing deadlines and propose a manageable schedule.

title: Set up a quiet homework space
subtitle: Keep supplies ready and distractions away
description: Provide a well-lit workspace with needed materials, and reduce distractions such as television and phone calls.

ageVersions.title: Help your child organise their homework supplies and remove distractions
ageVersions.subtitle: Practise together; let your child take the next step
ageVersions.description: Set up the space together and let them get it ready for study.

ageVersions.title: Agree with your teen on a study space and how to limit distractions
ageVersions.subtitle: Plan together and let your teen take more responsibility
ageVersions.description: Let them choose a workable space and discuss occasional check-ins.

ageVersions.title: Let your teen manage their study environment and ask for changes that help
ageVersions.subtitle: Support self-management and remain available to help
ageVersions.description: Discuss what interrupts their work and support their plan to reduce it.

title: Divide a large assignment into smaller parts
subtitle: Plan manageable work sessions
description: Help your child break a big assignment into sections and make a schedule for completing them.

ageVersions.title: Break a big assignment into steps with your child
ageVersions.subtitle: Practise together; let your child take the next step
ageVersions.description: Write the steps together and let your child choose where to start.

ageVersions.title: Ask your teen to draft the steps and deadlines for a large assignment
ageVersions.subtitle: Plan together and let your teen take more responsibility
ageVersions.description: Review their plan together before they begin.

ageVersions.title: Let your teen plan a large assignment and adjust the schedule as they go
ageVersions.subtitle: Support self-management and remain available to help
ageVersions.description: Check in at agreed points and help if the workload becomes unmanageable.

title: Let your child see you reading a book for enjoyment
subtitle: Model an interest in learning
description: Let your child see you reading for yourself, so reading is something adults enjoy as well as a school task.

title: Help your child invite a friend over to play
subtitle: Let them choose whom to invite and coordinate with the other parent.
description: Ask your school-age child whom they would like to invite, then coordinate with the other parent. Give the children space to play while remaining available.

title: Play a card or board game to teach your child to take turns
subtitle: Explain each turn and help when waiting is difficult.
description: Play a suitable card or board game and explain whose turn comes next. Offer support while your child learns, instead of requiring independent turn-taking immediately.

title: Respect your child’s choice to refuse a hug or kiss
subtitle: Support their right to say no to unwanted touch
description: Explain that they can refuse unwanted touch, even from familiar people. Respect their answer when offering affection.

title: Practise how your child can leave bullying and get adult help
subtitle: Discuss speaking up when safe, walking away and telling a trusted adult.
description: Discuss what your child can do if bullied: speak firmly if safe, move away when it is not, and seek help from a trusted adult.

title: Help your child repair the harm if they have bullied someone
subtitle: Choose a response linked to the harm, such as repairing damaged belongings.
description: Only when your child has bullied someone: involve them in an appropriate repair, such as fixing damaged property or writing an apology. Do not force a meeting with the child who was harmed.

title: Teach your child to ask before borrowing someone else’s belongings
subtitle: Wait for permission before taking the item
description: Model asking to use someone else’s things and waiting for their answer. Remind your child of the same rule when needed.

title: Let your teen explain their view before you respond in a disagreement
subtitle: Listen without insults or interruptions
description: When you disagree, hear your teen’s perspective calmly before explaining yours. Focus on the issue rather than personal criticism.

title: Teach your child to tell a trusted adult about touch or secrets that worry them
subtitle: Make clear that speaking up is allowed
description: Explain that they can tell a trusted adult about anything that worries or upsets them, even if someone asked them to keep it secret.

title: Volunteer with your child in an activity suitable for their age
subtitle: Choose a community activity where you can help together.
description: Include your child in a suitable community activity, such as helping with a food-bank meal. Choose an opportunity that welcomes children and fits their abilities.

title: Invite your teen’s friends over so you can get to know them
subtitle: Make friends welcome in your home
description: Create opportunities to meet the friends your teen spends time with, including welcoming them into your home.

title: Talk with your teen about caring behaviour and controlling behaviour in relationships
subtitle: Discuss personal choices, friendships, pressure and respectful disagreement.
description: With your teen, discuss being able to keep friendships, make choices and disagree safely. Explain how controlling behaviour differs from care.

title: Tell your child exactly what you appreciated about their effort
subtitle: Name the action you noticed
description: Describe a specific effort or helpful action rather than giving a general label about the child.

title: Let your child do their own homework
subtitle: Offer guidance without taking over
description: Be available to explain or suggest an approach, while letting your child do the thinking and complete the work themselves.

ageVersions.title: Let your child attempt homework before you offer a hint
ageVersions.subtitle: Practise together; let your child take the next step
ageVersions.description: Explain instructions when needed; leave the thinking and answers to them.

ageVersions.title: Ask what your teen has tried before helping with homework
ageVersions.subtitle: Plan together and let your teen take more responsibility
ageVersions.description: Offer guidance on the sticking point without completing the work.

ageVersions.title: Encourage your teen to ask their teacher for help with persistent homework difficulties
ageVersions.subtitle: Support self-management and remain available to help
ageVersions.description: Help them identify the question and support them in seeking help.

title: Ask your child to show you the apps and games they use
subtitle: Learn what they do there and how they interact with other people.
description: Let your child walk you through a platform they use so you understand its features and how they interact with others there.

title: Agree on screen-use limits together
subtitle: Include screen-free times in your family media plan.
description: Create a family media plan with expectations and limits suited to your child. Agree on screen-free times such as meals, homework and bedtime, and have adults follow the plan too.

ageVersions.title: Make screen-use rules with your child and practise following them
ageVersions.subtitle: Practise together; let your child take the next step
ageVersions.description: Agree screen-free times and explain how the family will follow the plan.

ageVersions.title: Negotiate a family media plan with your teen
ageVersions.subtitle: Plan together and let your teen take more responsibility
ageVersions.description: Include their priorities while protecting sleep, schoolwork and meals.

ageVersions.title: Review your teen’s media plan together and adjust limits that are not working
ageVersions.subtitle: Support self-management and remain available to help
ageVersions.description: Have them explain how their plan protects responsibilities, sleep and relationships.

title: Point out advertisements while watching online content with your child
subtitle: Explain when a video or influencer is promoting something.
description: When viewing content together, help your child distinguish advertising, edited material and an influencer’s promotional message.

title: Use anatomical names when answering your child’s questions about their body
subtitle: Speak calmly and use words they can understand
description: Use correct anatomical terms calmly when discussing the body or answering your child’s questions.

title: Agree where your child is going and when they will check in
subtitle: Discuss companions and how to contact each other
description: Agree where your child is going, who they will be with, and when and how they will check in.

title: Check your child’s car seat, booster or seatbelt before every trip
subtitle: Use the restraint that fits their age and size
description: Follow the seat and vehicle instructions. Use a rear-facing seat until its size limit, then a harnessed forward-facing seat, then a booster until the belt fits properly. Keep children under 13 in the back seat.

title: Check your child’s helmet fit and straps before each bike or scooter ride
subtitle: Use a helmet designed for the activity
description: Use an age-appropriate, certified helmet for cycling or a non-motorised scooter. Check fit, condition and fastening before riding.

title: Set up privacy and messaging controls before your child uses a new account
subtitle: Review who can contact them, reporting tools and purchase permissions.
description: When an age-appropriate account is created, use secure privacy settings and discuss who can contact them, reporting tools and purchase permissions. Explain why passwords should not be shared with friends.

title: Ask permission before sharing someone’s photo
subtitle: Respect a no or a change of mind
description: Ask the people pictured before sharing their photo or video. Remove it if they later ask you to.

title: Tell your child they can show you upsetting online messages without getting blamed
subtitle: Listen calmly when they ask for help
description: Make clear that your child can seek help for online experiences, even after a mistake. If they disclose something upsetting, listen and help them work out the next step.

title: Explain to your teen that consent must be freely given and can change
subtitle: No pressure, assumptions or continuing after someone says stop
description: Discuss asking before sexual touching, respecting a refusal and stopping if someone changes their mind or seems unsure. Agreement to one activity does not mean agreement to another.

title: Agree how your teen can contact you to leave a situation involving alcohol or drugs
subtitle: Practise refusing an offer and choose a message or code word for help.
description: With your teen, practise declining an offer and agree on an exit plan, such as a code word they can text a family member.

title: Answer your child’s puberty questions without teasing
subtitle: Use factual, age-appropriate explanations
description: Listen to the question and answer plainly. If you do not know, say so and find reliable information together. Let your child choose another trusted adult if they prefer.

title: Explain puberty changes before your child experiences them
subtitle: Ask what they already know and correct misunderstandings
description: Discuss changes such as body hair, a changing voice or periods in simple, factual language. Explain that timing varies; ask a healthcare professional about concerns over unusually early or delayed development.

title: Check that your teen has the toiletries they need
subtitle: Keep washing and personal-care products accessible
description: Ask privately whether your teen needs soap, deodorant, skin-care or menstrual products, and make suitable supplies available.

title: Explain periods and help your child pack spare menstrual products
subtitle: Prepare before their first period
description: Talk about periods before they begin, and help your child keep spare menstrual products and underwear somewhere accessible.

title: Explain what will happen if a rule is broken, then follow through calmly
subtitle: Use a realistic consequence and give a chance to respond
description: State the rule and a manageable consequence. Give your child a chance to change the behaviour and follow through calmly if necessary.

title: Apologise to your child after shouting or treating them unfairly
subtitle: Own your behaviour and explain what you will do differently.
description: When you make a parenting mistake, acknowledge it, apologise without shifting blame, and explain how you intend to do better.

title: Tell your child you love them even when they make a mistake
subtitle: Keep affection separate from achievement
description: Let your child know they are loved through words and affection, including when they have made a mistake.

title: Knock and wait before entering your teen’s room
subtitle: Respect everyday privacy
description: Knock before entering and ask before looking through personal belongings. Discuss privacy expectations together.

title: Let your toddler choose between two options you can accept
subtitle: Use simple choices such as which shirt to wear
description: Offer two suitable options and give your toddler time to choose. Use choices for decisions they can make.

title: Agree on household rules with your teen
subtitle: Discuss expectations and consequences together
description: Involve your teenager in setting family rules and the consequences of breaking them.

title: Offer a different activity when your child starts getting frustrated
subtitle: Redirect early, before the situation escalates
description: When you notice restlessness or frustration building, suggest a change of activity. If your child has hurt someone or is already overwhelmed, address safety and help them settle first.

title: Take slow breaths before responding when you feel angry with your child
subtitle: Pause while keeping your child safe
description: When your anger rises, pause and breathe slowly before responding. Keep your child safely supervised during the pause.

title: Follow through on a promise you make to your child
subtitle: Promise only what you can realistically do
description: When you agree to do something with or for your child, follow through. Make commitments you can keep.

title: Make a morning checklist with your child and tick off completed steps
subtitle: Use words or pictures they can follow
description: List the steps of getting ready together. Let your child mark each step as it is finished, with help as needed.

ageVersions.title: Let your child follow their morning checklist before you check together
ageVersions.subtitle: Practise together; let your child take the next step
ageVersions.description: Have them tick off the steps, then review anything missed together.

ageVersions.title: Help your teen write a morning checklist and use their own reminders
ageVersions.subtitle: Plan together and let your teen take more responsibility
ageVersions.description: Let them choose the reminder system and review where they still need help.

ageVersions.title: Let your teen manage getting ready and leaving on time
ageVersions.subtitle: Support self-management and remain available to help
ageVersions.description: Agree the departure time; let them plan backwards and request support when needed.

title: Plan breaks during longer homework sessions
subtitle: Balance focused work with rest
description: Help your child schedule breaks when homework needs a longer work session.

ageVersions.title: Plan homework breaks with your child before a long session
ageVersions.subtitle: Practise together; let your child take the next step
ageVersions.description: Agree where breaks fit and help them return to the task.

ageVersions.title: Ask your teen to include breaks in their study plan
ageVersions.subtitle: Plan together and let your teen take more responsibility
ageVersions.description: Let them plan rest alongside work, with support if restarting is difficult.

ageVersions.title: Encourage your teen to adjust study breaks when concentration drops
ageVersions.subtitle: Support self-management and remain available to help
ageVersions.description: Help them review whether their work-and-rest pattern is effective.

title: Use a visual timer to show your child how much task time remains
subtitle: Offer this support when they struggle to judge passing time.
description: For a child who struggles with time management, use a visual timer or countdown clock during a task so they can see how much time remains.

title: Put finished homework in the school bag
subtitle: Complete the final step before moving on
description: After checking the work is complete, place it in the appropriate folder and school bag.

ageVersions.title: Have your child pack completed work, then check the bag together
ageVersions.subtitle: Practise together; let your child take the next step
ageVersions.description: Let them use their school checklist before your final check.

ageVersions.title: Let your teen check their timetable and pack the next day’s materials
ageVersions.subtitle: Plan together and let your teen take more responsibility
ageVersions.description: Agree a reminder system rather than packing for them.

ageVersions.title: Let your teen manage bringing and submitting completed schoolwork
ageVersions.subtitle: Support self-management and remain available to help
ageVersions.description: Help them choose a tracking system if papers or submissions are being missed.

title: Ask how your child feels about an upcoming event
subtitle: Let them name concerns without suggesting fears
description: Ask an open question about the event and listen. Avoid questions that assume something frightening will happen.

title: Help your child plan what to do if a situation they worry about happens
subtitle: Work through a practical response together
description: Discuss the specific worry and who or what could help if it happened. Keep the conversation focused on coping rather than guarantees.

ageVersions.title: Help your child make a coping plan for a specific worry
ageVersions.subtitle: Practise together; let your child take the next step
ageVersions.description: Name the situation and identify who can help.

ageVersions.title: Ask your teen what they could do if the situation they fear happened
ageVersions.subtitle: Plan together and let your teen take more responsibility
ageVersions.description: Help them build a realistic coping plan without promising certainty.

ageVersions.title: Let your teen choose coping steps and the support they want for a worry
ageVersions.subtitle: Support self-management and remain available to help
ageVersions.description: Listen, discuss realistic options and agree when they would ask for more help.

title: Help your nervous child join a group game at their own pace
subtitle: Start with watching, then moving closer if ready
description: Let your child observe before joining. Encourage manageable steps towards playing with others and recognise their effort. Slow down if they become overwhelmed.

title: Use the same brief goodbye when leaving your child at nursery or school
subtitle: Explain when you will return
description: Give your child your attention, use a familiar goodbye and explain your return using an event they understand. Follow through on the plan.

title: Help arguing siblings take turns explaining the problem and agree on a solution
subtitle: Wait until they can talk calmly
description: Hear each child’s view without interruption, help them suggest solutions and agree on a workable plan.

title: Agree on turns before siblings use a shared game or device
subtitle: Make the order predictable
description: Help siblings agree who uses a shared item first and when turns change. Put the plan somewhere they can check.

title: Tell your children what you appreciated when they helped each other
subtitle: Name the helpful action between siblings
description: When siblings cooperate or help each other, describe the action you appreciated so they know what worked.

title: Choose a regular homework time that fits your child
subtitle: Allow for a snack or play beforehand if helpful
description: Agree on a study time that suits your child; some work better after a snack and play, while others prefer later.

title: Teach your child to help fold the clean laundry
subtitle: Show the steps and work together
description: Demonstrate folding suitable items and let your child help with the family laundry. Give support as they learn.

ageVersions.title: Let your child fold and put away their clean clothes
ageVersions.subtitle: Practise together; let your child take the next step
ageVersions.description: Show difficult folds and let them finish what they can.

ageVersions.title: Teach your teen to sort, wash and put away laundry
ageVersions.subtitle: Plan together and let your teen take more responsibility
ageVersions.description: Demonstrate machine settings and safe use of laundry products.

ageVersions.title: Let your teen manage their laundry from washing to putting it away
ageVersions.subtitle: Support self-management and remain available to help
ageVersions.description: Agree access to shared equipment and help with unfamiliar fabrics.

title: Ask your child what they want you to discuss at their teacher meeting
subtitle: Take their questions and concerns into the conversation.
description: Before a primary-school teacher meeting, ask what your child wants discussed. Take those questions along and ask how you can support learning at home.

title: Help your child choose something to save for and plan how to afford it
subtitle: For ages 6–9, connect saving with a specific goal.
description: For ages 6–9, help your child identify a specific savings goal and make a plan to reach it.
